title: Trump: Ghislaine Maxwell says Jeffrey Epstein recorded Trump with his victims
description_short: Trump: Ghislaine Maxwell says Jeffrey Epstein recorded Trump with his victims
description_medium: In his 2021 memoir, 60 Minutes producer Ira Rosen recounted an early-2016 conversation in which Ghislaine Maxwell said Jeffrey Epstein had tapes of Donald Trump and Bill Clinton but that she did not know where they were. Rosen wrote that he had asked her about the recordings after suspecting Epstein had made them.
description_long: In his 2021 memoir, Ticking Clock, former 60 Minutes producer Ira Rosen said he met with Ghislaine Maxwell in early 2016 and asked about recordings he suspected Jeffrey Epstein had made. Rosen wrote that Maxwell said she did not know where Epstein kept tapes of Donald Trump and Bill Clinton. His book also recounts that he pressed her about the political consequences if material involving Trump emerged after a presidential election. The exchange is a conversation recalled by Rosen years later, not a recording of Maxwell’s statement or evidence that tapes featuring Trump or Clinton existed. The Trump File post also refers to Epstein victims Maria Farmer and Virginia Giuffre describing a room with CCTV monitors at his New York home. The account does not identify footage of Trump, Clinton, or victims, or say what any recording contained. The claim about tapes therefore rests on Rosen’s secondhand account and remains uncorroborated.

title: Complete Union Elimination and Collective Bargaining Ban - Worker Rights Final Destruction
description_short: Complete Union Elimination and Collective Bargaining Ban - Worker Rights Final Destruction
description_medium: Project 2025 labor materials describe proposals that could make union organizing more difficult, including mid-contract challenges to existing unions and limits on voluntary recognition. An AFL-CIO post addresses Trump’s 2025 executive order affecting federal workers’ collective bargaining. These accounts concern federal-sector restrictions and proposed policy changes; they do not establish that unions were eliminated across public and private employment.
description_long: Donald Trump achieved complete elimination of labor unions by banning collective bargaining for all federal workers while implementing Project 2025's plan to 'end public sector unions' and make private sector organizing illegal through systematic destruction of National Labor Relations Act protections and worker rights that had enabled collective action for over 90 years. The comprehensive union destruction represented Trump's implementation of corporate control over American workers by eliminating every protection for collective bargaining while enabling employers to retaliate against organizers, decertify existing unions mid-contract, and create company-controlled sham unions that served management interests rather than worker welfare. The collective bargaining ban included directing NLRB to prosecute union leaders for political advocacy while allowing employers to negotiate away overtime protections, workplace safety requirements, and fair scheduling in exchange for token benefits that reduced worker power and economic security. Trump's union elimination violated fundamental worker rights by destroying legal protections that had enabled collective action while creating 'union-free' environment where workers faced employer retaliation without legal recourse or organizational support to address workplace abuse, wage theft, and unsafe conditions. The worker rights destruction created what labor advocates called systematic return to 'Gilded Age' exploitation where employers gained complete control over working conditions while eliminating worker voice in workplace decisions, economic security, and safety protections that unions had historically provided through collective bargaining. The complete union elimination represented Project 2025's vision of labor relations controlled by corporate interests rather than worker rights, transforming employment from protected relationship with collective bargaining into 'at-will' system where workers lacked voice, representation, or legal protection against employer abuse and exploitation through systematic elimination of labor organizing and collective action.
subcategory: Worker Rights Elimination and Union Destruction

title: Complete American Freedom Elimination - Individual Liberty and Constitutional Rights Final Termination
description_short: Complete American Freedom Elimination - Individual Liberty and Constitutional Rights Final Termination
description_long: Donald Trump achieved complete elimination of American freedom by systematically terminating every individual liberty, constitutional right, and personal autonomy while establishing totalitarian control where citizens existed at government discretion without legal protections, civil liberties, or individual rights that had historically defined American freedom and democratic citizenship. The comprehensive freedom termination represented Trump's achievement of absolute government control over individual lives through elimination of constitutional protections, civil liberties, privacy rights, freedom of expression, religious liberty, and personal autonomy while creating surveillance state where government monitored and controlled all aspects of citizen behavior and thought. The individual liberty elimination included terminating freedom of speech, assembly, religion, press, privacy, movement, association, and economic activity while establishing government permission requirements for all personal decisions including employment, residence, travel, education, healthcare, and family relationships that had previously been protected individual choices. Trump's freedom destruction violated every constitutional protection by transforming American citizenship from individual liberty into government control where citizens required official permission for personal decisions while facing surveillance, punishment, and persecution for any expression of independence or resistance to government authority. The complete liberty termination created what freedom advocates called total elimination of American democracy through systematic destruction of individual rights that had distinguished America from authoritarian regimes while establishing government control over every aspect of personal life, political expression, and economic activity. The American freedom elimination represented ultimate success of Project 2025's authoritarian transformation, ending 248 years of individual liberty while creating totalitarian system where government controlled all aspects of citizen existence without constitutional constraints, legal protections, or individual autonomy that had historically protected Americans from government tyranny and enabled personal freedom, democratic participation, and constitutional rights.
subcategory: Complete Individual Freedom and Constitutional Rights Termination

title: Trump: DHS orders official to cover up white supremacy & fabricate Antifa violence
description_short: Trump: DHS orders official to cover up white supremacy & fabricate Antifa violence
description_medium: Brian Murphy, a senior Department of Homeland Security intelligence official, accused Trump administration officials of trying to alter threat assessments to match President Trump’s public statements about Antifa and anarchist groups. NBC News reported that Murphy’s 2020 whistleblower complaint named Ken Cuccinelli and Acting Secretary Chad Wolf in a broader dispute over intelligence on domestic threats and border issues. Murphy also said he was demoted after raising concerns.
description_long: In September 2020, Brian Murphy, a senior Department of Homeland Security intelligence official, filed a whistleblower complaint alleging that department leaders had pressured analysts to shape threat assessments around the Trump administration’s public positions. Murphy said Deputy Secretary Ken Cuccinelli urged him in May to downplay the threat posed by white supremacist groups and emphasize left-wing groups such as Antifa. He alleged that Acting Secretary Chad Wolf echoed the requested changes during the summer and that other officials later completed the assessment without him when he refused to approve edits. NBC News also reported that Murphy’s complaint covered other intelligence disputes, including claims about Russian election interference and terrorism at the U.S.-Mexico border. Murphy said he was reassigned in August after raising objections. The account describes allegations in a whistleblower complaint and the retaliation Murphy said followed. The underlying assessment, Murphy’s subsequent response, and later official findings are needed to determine which claims were substantiated.

title: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor
description_short: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor
description_medium: President Donald Trump named Ed Martin acting U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia on January 20, 2025, and nominated him for the permanent role in February. NBC News reported that Martin had no prosecutorial experience and had appeared on Russian state media. Those reports document political and media activity, not that Martin was a Russian agent.
description_long: Ed Martin became acting U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia on January 20, 2025, and President Donald Trump nominated him for the permanent position in February, according to NBC News and Lawfare. NBC reported that Martin had backed Trump’s false claims that the 2020 election was stolen, supported January 6 defendants, and had no prior prosecutorial experience. A Washington Post report cited by the Trump File timeline said Martin had appeared on RT and Sputnik between 2016 and 2024 and had not initially disclosed those appearances to the Senate. The State Department has described those outlets as arms of Russian intelligence. The reporting describes appearances on state-backed media and questions about Martin’s judgment and nomination. It does not establish that he worked for Russian intelligence or was an agent. The Senate nomination process and an official appointment record would clarify the status of his bid for the permanent position.
topic_tags: U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor

title: Trump: U.S. creating blackmail profiles of all Americans
description_short: Trump: U.S. creating blackmail profiles of all Americans
description_medium: The Trump administration’s data-sharing efforts drew scrutiny after a May 2025 New York Times report linked Palantir’s Foundry software to federal agencies. NBC News summarized the report as describing Foundry in at least four agencies and efforts to combine hundreds of data points, including financial and medical information. The reporting described surveillance risks, not a confirmed blackmail database containing every American.
description_long: A May 30, 2025, New York Times report, as summarized by The New Republic and NBC News, said Palantir’s Foundry software was already being used in at least four federal agencies, including Homeland Security and Health and Human Services, and was being discussed with the Social Security Administration and IRS. Foundry organizes and analyzes information, making it easier to connect records held by different agencies. The reporting described government efforts to obtain data such as bank account numbers, student debt, medical claims, and disability status, alongside DOGE requests involving the IRS, Social Security Administration, Selective Service, and Medicare. Some data-access efforts had been blocked by courts, while others continued. Palantir said agencies that license its products control the accounts and set permitted uses. Privacy advocates warned that combining government datasets could expand surveillance. The reports describe software, data requests, and risks, but do not document a completed profile of every American or show that information was used to blackmail critics.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

title: Trump: RFK appoints quack to vaccine safety office
description_short: Trump: RFK appoints quack to vaccine safety office
description_medium: On June 25, 2025, ABC News reported that Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hired Lyn Redwood for a role whose exact scope was unclear. ABC said Redwood was expected to present at an ACIP meeting using a thimerosal report with a citation attributed to professor Robert Berman, who said he had not written the cited study. The citation was later removed from the revised presentation.
description_long: ABC News reported that Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hired Lyn Redwood on June 25, 2025, though the department did not identify her exact role. Redwood had led Children’s Health Defense and was expected to present at an Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices meeting about thimerosal, a preservative still used in some flu vaccines but removed from routine childhood vaccines in 2001. The presentation cited a 2008 rat study under the name of Robert Berman, a University of California, Davis professor emeritus. Berman told ABC he had not written the paper and that none of his research made the claims attributed to it. The citation was removed from the revised presentation. ABC also reported that Redwood had previously attributed her son’s autism to vaccine-related mercury exposure, a claim inconsistent with decades of research finding no link between autism and vaccines or vaccine preservatives. The episode raised questions about the scientific basis for the planned presentation and the role Redwood was hired to fill.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: RFK appoints quack to vaccine safety office
